nodes.name: The Twilight Order
nodes.summary: Secret order, concealed for countless centuries, that rebuilt Oriath while the world believed it abandoned. It aims to free mankind from the 'tyranny of the gods' and build a god-free 'Utopia'; behind the scenes it is plotting to create a new Beast and trigger another Cataclysm. Led by the Countess (Oriana).

chronology.relative: Hidden for centuries; active ~20 years after the end of PoE1 (PoE1 present is ~1620 IC)

sources.locator: intro quote (Path of Exile 2 Art Book): 'The Twilight Order, however, did not flee. They emerged from countless centuries of secrecy to rebuild Oriath's heart'
intro: 'leader of the Twilight Order... plotting to create a new Beast and start another Cataclysm'
Confront Kanu and the First Herald: Countess 'The Twilight Order will see to it that the world is remade. A world without gods... without suffering... without the disease of Divinity.'

nodes.name: The Edicts (Precursor murals)
nodes.summary: Series of vague Precursor murals described by the PoE2 wiki as depicting the Beast and possibly instructions on how to contain it; numbered First to Fourth in game. Known: Third = instrument is the Weapon (Hooded One recognises it as 'the Weapon I saw in that third mural'); Second = Doryani's guess that the Seed was its instrument; Fourth = investigated in the Epilogue after the Arbiter of Ash (PoE1 wiki editors speculate it caused the Great Fire); First = unexplained threat averted in the Epilogue. The full text of the edicts is not given in any source read. Not to be confused with Count Geonor's hanging edicts in Ogham.

chronology.relative: Precursor age, far older than the Vaal and Winter of the World

sources.locator: 'It was depicted in their Edicts, vague murals that depicts the Beast and possibly instructions on how to contain it.'
Return to Kingsmarch: Doryani 'The Third Edict? What is the meaning... of these Edicts?'
Return to Kingsmarch: Hooded One 'It is the Weapon I saw in that third mural'; Enter the Excavated Site: Makoru 'These murals... appear to depict the Weapon... and the Beast'

nodes.name: The First Edict
nodes.summary: Unexplained so far. Tecrod, hunting for the Edicts, is destroyed by the Arbiter of Divinity with 'Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!'; on completing the Epilogue quest Legacy of the Precursors the log reads 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.' Its contents are not described in sources read; 'ordain' implies it is something that can be enacted or activated, and the Origin Tower / Origin Core are the setting.

sources.locator: Lore: 'Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!'
Quest Complete: 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.'

nodes.name: The Second Edict
nodes.summary: Never shown directly. Only Doryani's speculation, after the Third Edict is revealed: 'Perhaps it follows that the Seed was the instrument of a Second Edict... Why would any civilisation intentionally create the Seed of Corruption?'

sources.locator: Return to Kingsmarch: Doryani 'Perhaps it follows that the Seed was the instrument of a Second Edict...'

nodes.name: The Third Edict
nodes.summary: Precursor edict whose instrument is the Weapon. After the Hooded One reforges it, the inscription reads 'The instrument of the Third Edict'; the Weapon was 'designed for the sole purpose of cleansing Corruption... and destroying the Beast'. Revealed in Act 4 (0.3.0, whose update bears the name 'The Third Edict'). The Hooded One's wording ('that third mural') implies the edicts are murals he had seen in the Excavated Site.

sources.locator: Return to Kingsmarch: Hooded One 'It is the Weapon I saw in that third mural. The forging revealed an inscription. The symbols declare it The instrument of the Third Edict.'
Version history 0.3.0: 'The instrument of the Third Edict. Journey to Kingsmarch...'

nodes.name: The Fourth Edict
nodes.summary: Mystery edict. In Legacy of the Precursors (Epilogue quest, 0.5.0) the step 'Investigate the Fourth Edict' follows the defeat of the Arbiter of Ash at the Burning Monolith (quest-log step 102, preserved in a commented section of the wiki page). The Arbiter of Ash reportedly voices 'The Fourth Edict beckons' (reported via search snippet of the PoE2 wiki page, not verified directly). The PoE1 wiki states the Great Fire / Winter of the World 'was likely caused by the Fourth Edict, a contingency created by the Precursors to purge Wraeclast in flames' (wiki editors' inference); a Quora answer reads it as the Flame Seed the Arbiter wields and which is stolen. The edict's actual text is not verified; Talkative Tri's 'The Fourth Edict - Path of Exile 2 Lore Mysteries' video (zIhWe5lLGKs) transcript could not be retrieved.

sources.locator: The Great Fire: 'likely caused by the Fourth Edict, a contingency created by the Precursors to purge Wraeclast in flames'
quote 'The Fourth Edict beckons' (flaming orb attack) - reported via search result, unverified locally
fan answer: fourth edict = flame seed (speculation)

nodes.name: Count Geonor's Edicts (Ogham decrees)
nodes.summary: Notices posted across Ogham by Count Geonor declaring all crimes punishable by hanging, bodies thrown into a pit beneath his manor; a 'notice of criminality' is found near Clearfell. Not Precursor edicts; the executions fed the Beast seed/creature in the manor cage.

sources.locator: [0:25]-[0:41] 'The count's edicts posted throughout the island declared that all crimes were now punishable by hanging'; [4:25]-[4:36]

nodes.name: Geonor's Journal
nodes.summary: Environmental lore in Ogham Manor: Geonor writes that Oriana 'assures me, we can right some of the wrongs of the past' and promises a way forward for Ogham, showing how the Countess recruited him.

nodes.name: The Countess (Oriana)
nodes.summary: Major PoE2 antagonist and leader of the Twilight Order. Manipulates Count Geonor and Jamanra to obtain and feed the Beast, abandoning them when useless; has a son, Lumerius, whom she intends to use in her agenda.

sources.locator: Confront Kanu and the First Herald

nodes.name: Lumerius
nodes.summary: Son of the Countess whom she 'seeks to use to fulfill her agenda'. His role in the Order is not clarified in any source read.

sources.locator: paragraph 2: 'She also has a son named Lumerius'

nodes.name: The Saviour
nodes.summary: Figure the Twilight Order's followers swear oaths to and invoke ('For the Saviourrr!', 'Embrace the saviour! Pledge now'); listed first among Order members. Identity/nature not revealed in sources read.

nodes.name: Benedictus, First Herald of Utopia
nodes.summary: Twilight Order herald and boss of The Excavation in Act 4. Demands the weapon pieces from the Exile and Kanu, tries to bury them to cover the Countess's retreat.

sources.locator: Defeat Benedictus: 'My lady... you must take your leave! ... For the Saviourrr!'

nodes.name: Torvian, Hand of the Saviour
nodes.summary: Twilight Order champion and boss of Arastas in Act 4, defeated while the Exile searches for a way to reforge the Weapon.

sources.locator: Arastas boss: Torvian, Hand of the Saviour
Defeat Torvian, Hand of the Saviour

nodes.name: Servitor Marius
nodes.summary: Twilight Order member on Arastas who invites the player to join their Utopia or donate; refused.

nodes.name: Missionary Lorandis
nodes.summary: Twilight Order preacher in Kingsmarch who sends the Exile to Arastas to take an oath to the Saviour and later leads them to the Herald; cries 'We were trying to... save you' when the ambush turns.

sources.locator: Follow the Preacher / Survive the ambush

nodes.name: Vel Anxa
nodes.summary: Priest 'of the Order' listed as a Twilight Order member under Torvian, Hand of the Saviour. No further detail in sources read.

nodes.name: Herius
nodes.summary: Priest 'of the Order' listed as a Twilight Order member under Torvian, Hand of the Saviour. No further detail in sources read.

nodes.name: Cnaeus
nodes.summary: Priest 'of the Order' listed as a Twilight Order member under Torvian, Hand of the Saviour. No further detail in sources read.

nodes.name: Kanu
nodes.summary: First Mate of the Aurora May, listed among Twilight Order members: he is courted by Benedictus ('Accept Utopia!'), betrays Makoru, then reveals the Beast is kept in Oriath and is attacked by Tavakai ('Let the ancestors judge him') - death is implied.

sources.locator: Confront Kanu and the First Herald; Defeat Benedictus

nodes.name: Makoru
nodes.summary: Captain of the Aurora May, Karui, daughter of Tavakai; betrayed by Kanu and taken by her father when he flees with the Weapon.

sources.locator: Talk to Makoru; Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon

nodes.name: Tecrod, the Hated Slave
nodes.summary: Abyssal Lich Lord ('the Hated Slave') with a white halo; unlike Amanamu, Kurgal and Ulaman he acts independently of Kulemak and hunts the Edicts. Appears as a wyrm rider who steals the Flame Seed after the Arbiter of Ash falls; when the Exile places the Origin Core in the Origin Tower his wyrm incapacitates the Exile and he claims the power for 'the Master', but the Arbiter of Divinity destroys his body.

nodes.name: The Arbiter of Divinity
nodes.summary: Pinnacle boss of the Origin Tower in the Epilogue (0.5.0); destroys Tecrod's body with 'Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!'. Nature/identity not established in sources read; fighting it ends the threat of the First Edict.

sources.locator: steps 139-141 Ascend the Tower / Place the Origin Core / Defeat the Arbiter of Divinity
0.5 pinnacle boss guide (new pinnacle boss, Return of the Ancients)

nodes.name: The Hooded One
nodes.summary: Mysterious guide of the PoE2 Exile, revealed in Act 2 to be the god Sin, the Thief of Virtue and creator of the Beast. Recognises Precursor writing from a mortal childhood memory, forges the Weapon, and in the Epilogue lies in corruption-induced sleep.

sources.locator: Speak to the Hooded One in the Shrine: 'I am... a god. I am the Thief of Virtue. I am Sin.'

nodes.name: The Weapon (Precursor Weapon)
nodes.summary: Three-piece Precursor device assembled in Act 4 on Arastas/Excavated Site; the instrument of the Third Edict, built to cleanse Corruption and destroy the Beast. Radiates intense Corruption, maddening those near it; Tavakai takes it, falls to blood fever, and is cured when the Hooded One uses it.

sources.locator: Speak to The Hooded One; Return to Kingsmarch
intro: 'search for three parts of the precursor weapon'

nodes.name: Seed of Corruption
nodes.summary: Precursor-made essence from which Sin created the Beast; stolen by Count Geonor at the start of PoE2, then carried by the Countess on the Dreadnought. Doryani speculates it was the instrument of a Second Edict.

sources.locator: Sin found a Precursor ruin containing the Seed of Corruption
Path of Exile 2 section: Sin took the Seed of Corruption into hiding; Geonor binds him and steals it

nodes.name: Flame Seed
nodes.summary: Precursor object guarded by the Arbiter of Ash; stolen by a mysterious wyrm rider (Tecrod) after the Arbiter's defeat. Possibly linked to the Fourth Edict (unconfirmed).

sources.locator: Lore: 'steals the Flame Seed after the Arbiter of Ash is defeated'
Precursor section: Arbiter of Ash created to guard the Flame Seed

nodes.name: Arastas
nodes.summary: Karui-archipelago island in Act 4 where the Twilight Order's church and Torvian are found; the Excavation lies beyond.

nodes.name: The Excavation
nodes.summary: Twilight Order dig site on Arastas, boss Benedictus; leads to the Excavated Site whose murals depict the Weapon and the Beast and where the Weapon is reforged.

sources.locator: Enter the Excavated Site: Makoru 'These murals... appear to depict the Weapon... and the Beast'

nodes.name: The Burning Monolith
nodes.summary: Endgame structure where the Arbiter of Ash is fought and the Fourth Edict is investigated, with the Origin Tower beyond it.

nodes.name: The Origin Tower
nodes.summary: Precursor tower reached via the Waygate in the Epilogue; the Exile places the Origin Core at the top, where Tecrod intervenes and the Arbiter of Divinity is fought.

nodes.name: Ogham Manor
nodes.summary: Count Geonor's seat in Act 1; the Beast seed was caged in its foundations and fed by hangings.

nodes.name: Utopia (Twilight Order ideal)
nodes.summary: The Order's promised god-free world ('without gods... without suffering... without the disease of Divinity'), recruited for with 'Accept Utopia! Embrace the saviour!'. Art book: intention is good but its methods are contentious.

nodes.name: Winter of the World (Great Fire / Great Wasting)
nodes.summary: Ancient cataclysm of ash, fire and Lightless invasion; PoE2 confirmed the Ezomyte Great Fire is the same event. PoE1 wiki says it was likely caused by the Fourth Edict.

sources.locator: Great Fire: 'revealed that the Great Fire was indeed the same event as the Winter of the World'

nodes.name: Oriath destroyed by Sirus
nodes.summary: PoE1 Conquerors of the Atlas: Oriath is completely destroyed by Sirus, leaving it devastated; PoE2 states the world believed Oriath abandoned twenty years ago after crises.

nodes.name: Twilight Order rebuilds Oriath
nodes.summary: After the abandonment, the Twilight Order emerged from secrecy and rebuilt Oriath in secret; Act 5 is set there and the Beast is held there (per Kanu).

sources.locator: intro: 'Oriath, which was rebuilt in secret'

nodes.name: The Forbidden Sanctum
nodes.summary: Templar catacombs under the Fellshrine Ruins (PoE1 Sanctum): lithomancy, necromancy and hidden truths of Innocence's ascension. Background for Oriathan Templar secrecy; no source ties it to the Twilight Order.

nodes.name: Path of Exile 2: The Third Edict (0.3.0)
nodes.summary: Content update launching Aug 29, 2025: Act 4 (Ngamakanui), three interludes, removal of Cruel, and Rise of the Abyssal league; named after the Weapon's Third Edict.

nodes.name: Geonor seizes the Seed from the Hooded One
nodes.summary: Opening cinematic: Count Geonor impales the Hooded One with a runic sword, takes the sphere holding the Seed of Corruption and shouts 'Bind him!'; Countess later reveals she was behind him.

nodes.name: Exile defeats Torvian

sources.locator: Defeat Torvian, Hand of the Saviour

nodes.name: Exile defeats Benedictus
nodes.summary: Act 4: after the Countess flees to Oriath, the Exile defeats Benedictus in the Excavation; Kanu then names Oriath and is killed by Tavakai.

nodes.name: The Weapon is reforged; Third Edict revealed
nodes.summary: The Hooded One reforges the Weapon in the Excavated Site; Tavakai seizes it. Back in Kingsmarch the Hooded One reads the inscription: 'The instrument of the Third Edict.'

sources.locator: Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon; Return to Kingsmarch

nodes.name: Hooded One recalls Precursor script
nodes.summary: Weapon pieces carry Precursor writing the Hooded One partly recognises from a mortal childhood: a book in a woman's lap, life 'somewhere else' with stone, metal and glass before being sent to the Azmeri with his brother and sister.

sources.locator: Witness The Hooded One (first and second pieces)

nodes.name: Siege of Oriath quest (Act 4 finale)
nodes.summary: Act 4 quest unlocked after the three Interludes: the Karui, Ezomytes, Maraketh and Vaal are united against the Twilight Order, but the attempt to sail to Oriath ends instead at the Ziggurat Refuge.

sources.locator: Quest Complete: 'If we do manage to stop the Twilight Order and slay the Beast...'

nodes.name: Legacy of the Precursors (Epilogue quest)
nodes.summary: 0.5.0 endgame quest: the Hooded One lies in corruption-induced sleep; Doryani leads the hunt through Enigma Chambers, Arbiter of Ash, Fourth Edict, Origin Tower, and the Arbiter of Divinity, ending 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.'

nodes.name: Arbiter of Ash defeated; Flame Seed stolen
nodes.summary: Precursor guardian of the Flame Seed falls in the Burning Monolith arena; a wyrm-riding figure (Tecrod) takes the Flame Seed, saying 'This power serves a new master...'.

nodes.name: Arbiter of Divinity destroys Tecrod; First Edict averted
nodes.summary: In the Origin Tower the Exile places the Origin Core; Tecrod's wyrm incapacitates the Exile and Tecrod exults 'With this, the Master shall know unending power!'; the Arbiter of Divinity destroys Tecrod's body ('Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!') and is then fought by the Exile (quest step 141).

nodes.name: Martyr of the First Edict (Void league leaderboard)
nodes.summary: Rise of the Abyssal mechanic: once per league a level-100 character can be sacrificed at the Site of the Chosen, sending it to the Void league and listing it as the 'Martyr of the First Edict' on the leaderboard. Meta/league flavour; no source explains the naming.

sources.locator: paragraph: 'listed as the Martyr of the First Edict on the leaderboard'

nodes.name: The Arbiter of Ash
nodes.summary: Precursor-created guardian of the Flame Seed and pinnacle boss of the Burning Monolith. After he falls a wyrm-riding figure (Tecrod) takes the Flame Seed; the Fourth Edict is investigated next. Little is known about him.

sources.locator: Precursors section: 'created the Arbiter of Ash (PoE 2) to guard the Flame Seed (PoE 2)'; 'Little is known about the Arbiter and the Flame Seed'
